story.title: Canada to Announce Retaliatory Tariffs Against U.S.
story.summary: Canada is set to announce retaliatory tariffs against the United States, according to an official familiar with the plans. This decision marks an escalation in a trade dispute that has intensified following the collapse of negotiations with the Trump administration.

related_stories.title: Trump Proposes 50% Tariffs on Canadian Vehicles Following Trade Talks Breakdown
related_stories.summary: President Trump has threatened to increase tariffs on Canadian vehicles to 50% after trade negotiations failed. He criticized Canada for perceived unfair trade practices, stating that the country has been 'ripping off' the U.S. for years. Economists warn that such tariffs could severely impact Canadian firms and threaten thousands of jobs in Canada.

related_stories.title: Trump Plans 50% Tariffs on Canadian Auto and Steel Imports Starting 2027
related_stories.summary: President Trump announced that tariffs on Canadian automotive and steel imports will increase to 50% starting January 1, 2027. This decision follows the failure of trade negotiations between the US and Canada. In response, Canada is preparing to impose retaliatory tariffs on US goods.

related_stories.title: Trump Considers Renaming Lake Ontario Amid Escalating Trade Tensions with Canada
related_stories.summary: Amid escalating trade tensions, Trump has suggested renaming Lake Ontario to 'Lake America.' He warned Canadian leaders to comply with U.S. demands or face consequences that could be 'far worse' than current tariffs. This rhetoric marks a significant increase in the ongoing trade dispute between the two nations.

related_stories.title: US Treasury Secretary Initiates 'Operation Economic Outcast' to Target Iran
related_stories.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced 'Operation Economic Outcast' aimed at isolating Iran economically. He stated that any entity facilitating money laundering for Iran would be excluded from the US dollar system. Concurrently, the Iranian rial fell to a record low of approximately 2.02 million to the dollar, as Bessent warned of an impending 'economic D-Day' for Iran.
